meta.name: Cyberhaven
meta.title: Cyberhaven ad teardown: a sharp DLP hook, an essay with no next step
meta.meta_desc: A teardown of Cyberhaven’s live LinkedIn ad: “What your DLP can’t see” is the sharpest line, it sits below a vague headline, and the click lands on an essay with no visible CTA.
meta.og_desc: The best line is buried. The page has no next step.

hook: The best line is buried in the ad.
The page has nowhere to go next.
voice.lede: “What your DLP can’t see” is the sharpest thing Cyberhaven says here, and it sits under a vaguer headline. The topic carries over well, since the ad and the page both talk about agentic AI outpacing legacy tools. But the click lands on a long thought-leadership essay with no CTA in the article itself, so a reader who agrees has nowhere to go but the navigation.

findings.title: A soft ask that fits the offer
findings.what: “See the shift” is a light CTA for a read, and that is the right size of ask for cold LinkedIn traffic.

findings.title: The headline hides the hook
findings.what: “AI Changed Work. We Protect It.” is clean but vague. “What your DLP can’t see” is the sharper line, and it sits in the body copy.
findings.fix: Lead the creative with “What your DLP can’t see.”

findings.title: Names the risk, not the answer
findings.what: “Your AI agents can now plan, act, and move data on their own” names the risk well. The ad never says what Cyberhaven does about it.
findings.fix: Add one line on what Cyberhaven sees that a DLP does not.

findings.title: The proof stayed on the page
findings.what: The ad has no named customer, stat or proof point. The most compelling number, a 60% adoption stat, only appears after the click.
findings.fix: Move that stat into the creative.

findings.title: A thousand words before the product
findings.what: The post runs past 1,000 words before any product specificity. Cyberhaven Flow gets one passing mention, with no screenshot and no capability list.
findings.fix: Show what the product sees, early, for the reader the DLP hook attracted.

findings.title: No next step
findings.what: The menu has a demo button, but the article itself has no CTA, just share buttons and an AI summary tool. Paid traffic reads, agrees and leaves.
findings.fix: Add one next step tied to the hook, like seeing what your DLP misses.

faq.q: What works in Cyberhaven’s LinkedIn ad?
faq.a: The topic and the ask. The ad and the page both center on agentic AI outpacing legacy tools, and a soft CTA fits a blog read.

faq.q: Can paid LinkedIn traffic go to a blog post?
faq.a: It can, if the post gives the reader a next step. An essay with no CTA in the article pays for attention it cannot keep.
Add a CTA inside the article. Then lead the creative with “What your DLP can’t see” and move the 60% stat into the ad.

issues.title: Headline Clarity
issues.explanation: 'AI Changed Work. We Protect It.' is clean but vague. 'What your DLP can't see' in the body copy is the sharper hook, buried.

issues.title: CTA Friction
issues.explanation: 'See the shift' as a soft content CTA fits a blog-read offer, low friction, appropriately light ask for cold LinkedIn traffic.

issues.title: Visual-Copy Match
issues.explanation: Abstract star shapes and flowing lines look nice but say nothing about data, agents, or security; pure decoration over the strong headline.

issues.title: Benefit Specificity
issues.explanation: 'Your AI agents can now plan, act, and move data on their own' names the risk well but never says what Cyberhaven actually does about it.

issues.title: Trust Signals
issues.explanation: No named customer, stat, or proof point in the creative itself; the compelling 60% adoption stat lives on the landing page, not the ad.
